2 How do the verb tenses change to express regret?
wish/If only for regrets
We use wish/if only to talk about regrets - things that
we would like to be different but that are impossible
or unlikely to change. If only tends to have 3 stronger
meaning than /wish.
We use:
wish/If only + the Past Simple for regrets in the present:
Iwish/If only + the Past Perfect for regrets about the past:
wish/If only + would when something or someone
does (or fails to do) something that annoys us. We'd like
it to change but we don't think it will.
Grammar Reference and Practice > page 186
WATCH OUT!
We use wish/if only would for things that we can't
change ourselves so we don't use them in the first
person:
wish yoU wouldn't do that. NOT twish Hwotldn't do that:
